changes: p1: the fragment '-radevo' is most likely [Śaṅka]radeva. Rajavamsi's reading of line 6 has 'śaṅkara-iti', and Śaṅkaradeva is the son of Vṛṣadeva in the Licchavi genealogy. Name given as Śaṅkaradeva (low confidence).
p2: 'devasuta' gives only the end of the father's name. Read as [Vṛṣa]deva (Vṛṣadeva), low confidence.
p1 roles: changed from king/donor to relative_only. Śaṅkaradeva appears in a genealogical eulogy as an ancestor. The donor and reigning king are not preserved by name.
Removed 'narendra' as a title of p1. It stands separately in a broken context and may refer to someone else.
Notes expanded: the possible link of Mānavihāra with Mānadeva, and that line 27 is not a date.

purpose: perpetual land grant (kṣetraṃ akṣayaṃ dattaṃ) to the Mānavihāra, with a eulogy of the royal line
notes:
The inscription is badly damaged.

Line 2: '. . . devasuta radevo' keeps only the endings of two names. Reading them as [Vṛṣa]devasuta [Śaṅka]radeva is a conjecture. It rests on Rajavamsi's reading 'śaṅkara-iti' in line 6 and on the known genealogy (Vṛṣadeva → Śaṅkaradeva → Dharmadeva → Mānadeva). Mānadeva is traditionally credited with founding the Mānavihāra, so the inscription may come from his reign or later. However, no reigning king, donor or recipient survives by name: 'rājā' appears only in line 13 and 'narendra' only in line 2.

Line 27, 'sāgraṃ śataṃ varṣāṇām', is part of the eulogy ('more than a hundred years'), not a date formula. No date survives.
